Based on the retrieved matches, it appears that detecting p53 alterations by immunohistochemistry (IHC) or single-strand conformation polymorphism analysis (SSCP) is not a clinically useful predictor of local response to pre-operative adjuvant therapy in advanced rectal cancer.

In other words, the presence or absence of p53 alterations does not provide a reliable indicator for predicting how well patients with locally advanced rectal cancer will respond to chemotherapy and radiation therapy before surgery. This suggests that further research is needed to better understand the relationship between p53 alterations and tumor response to these treatments.

Therefore, it seems that current evidence does not support using p53 alterations as a reliable predictor of local response to pre-operative chemo-radiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer.
